title: Preparing for Agent Compliance Regulations
summary: The AI Act's high-risk deadline moved to 2 December 2027, and the record-keeping obligations did not get easier. What Articles 12, 18, 19, 26 and 72 actually require, and the retention clocks to build now.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


**The deadline everyone planned around moved, and the obligation did not.** The AI Act's high-risk obligations for Annex III systems no longer land on 2 August 2026. The AI Omnibus amendment, which entered into force on 27 July 2026, pushed them to 2 December 2027, and Annex I systems embedded in regulated products to 2 August 2028.


Read the extension as time to build, not as a reprieve, because the demand underneath it is the one thing that cannot be produced retroactively. Article 12 requires high-risk systems to "technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system". Article 19 makes providers keep those logs for "at least six months", Article 26(6) puts the same floor on deployers, and Article 18 keeps the technical documentation for ten years after the system is placed on the market.


The common mistake is treating this as a legal project to start once the text settles. The text is settling now, in the direction of longer runways and unchanged evidence duties, and every month of unlogged agent activity is a month you can never describe.


We are not claiming an agent is automatically a high-risk system. Most are not. Annex III is specific, and the categories that catch enterprise agents are recruitment and worker management, creditworthiness, and access to essential services.


Start with the three clocks: a six-month minimum on logs, ten years on documentation, and post-market monitoring that runs "throughout their lifetime". Then make sure one query can return what one agent did on one day.
